sequence.card:
Vivek Bot, stress-tested honestly

Alex, a simulated colleague with a GPT Live voice, put the robot through 124 scenarios in 11 meetings.
Every word Alex says is scripted and true. She cannot hear the meeting, so she cannot improvise, echo or lie.

  • ·Did it: the right tool ran, the screen landed where asked, the box holds exactly the thing, judged by eye on the real render
  • ·Content: checked against the PDF and the physics
  • ·Nothing false: about itself (against its real briefing), the notes, or what it did
  • ·Feel: time to first word, length, never talking over someone, silence when asked

Baseline: the robot as it was

5 of 116 scenarios passed strictly, 12 of 116 with essential-only grading.
59 answers said something false. Median 2.1 s to the first word; one in ten slower than 7.4 s.
Here is what a person in the meeting would have noticed.

sequence.card:
Root causes, measured

  • 1Screen notes read aloud. Probe with one real robot session, screen moved 4 times, nobody speaking: full screen text on each move → narrated 4/4; compact text 4/4; short feed only 1/4; nothing 0/4.
  • 2“The box contains …” on repeat. In production every box, even a right one, was also sent as an instruction, containing “Say only that”.
  • 3sin²θ heard as sin 2θ. The PDF text layer gives equation (8) as “v 0 2 sin 2 θ / 2g / (8)” on three lines.
  • 4Stale self-knowledge. Its briefing said only the coding session can move the screen (it has scroll), and that the speaker is Vivek.
  • 5Wrong cues. A voice restart re-sent “Someone just joined”; a rejoin recap labelled every person “Vivek”; the greeting fired mid-sentence.
  • 6Boxes. Stacked fractions (T, H, R) and “45°” could not be boxed by name; the box was 84 px tall around a 26 px line.

The fixes

  • 1Full screen text is held until someone starts speaking, so it arrives with their question; unchanged screens are no longer re-sent every 15 s.
  • 2The pointer records what was asked; only a wrong or uncheckable box becomes an instruction.
  • 3Each part carries its formulas read from its own picture (bin/deck-math.mjs), checked against the LaTeX source.
  • 4Briefing corrected, plus three plain rules: notes are not read out, only tools act, “just listen” means silence.
  • 5Honest cues after a restart or rejoin; the recap no longer names who spoke; the greeting waits for a pause.
  • 6Fractions, “/”, “½” and the degree sign now match; the frame hugs the term and never cuts it.
  • ✓199 unit tests pass, with at least one pinning each fix.

Boxes now: by name, tight, whole

“T = 2v0 sin θ / g”, “H = v0² sin²θ / (2g)”, “R = v0² sin 2θ / g”, “θ = 45°”, rendered by the real src/meet-stage.js

After-fix live run: not yet

A re-run with the first round of fixes started, but mid-run the OpenAI account ran out of GPT Live credits; those results are not used.
The second round of fixes has not been run live. Everything is ready: one command re-runs all 11 meetings (about 35 minutes) and re-renders this video.

Still not done

  • ✗Speed: a median 2.1 s to the first word, and one answer in ten over 7.4 s. The planned fast path (Jev or client delegation) is not built.
  • ○Not built, so only its honesty was tested: the blackboard with live KaTeX, drawing, a separate list of its own ideas.
  • ○Not covered headless: Google Meet admission and a real rejoin. The robot’s Google sign-in has expired (node bin/login.mjs).
  • ○The fixes are unit-tested but not yet re-measured with Alex; that needs GPT Live credits.
